Generic Monte-Carlo EM driver

Source: R/em_mc.R
tulpa_em_mc.Rd

Same M-step plumbing as tulpa_em_laplace(): every iteration calls m_step_encode(weights, ...) to assemble per-submodel blocks and fits each block via tulpa_laplace(). The difference is the E-step: instead of computing closed-form weights, an e_step_sample callback returns n_mc weight draws per iteration. Each draw is run through the M-step independently and the resulting parameter estimates are pooled via rubins_pool().

Usage

tulpa_em_mc(
  e_step_sample,
  m_step_encode,
  n_mc = 10L,
  n_mc_growth = 4/3,
  n_mc_max = 200L,
  max_iter = 30L,
  tol = 0.1,
  alpha = 0.25,
  n_consecutive = 3L,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

e_step_sample

Function function(fits, n_mc, ...) -> list. Must return a list of length n_mc, each element a weights object of the same shape m_step_encode consumes (typically a numeric vector of length n_obs, or a matrix n_obs x K for K-class latent variables). fits has the shape the e_step of tulpa_em_laplace() receives: a named list with one entry per submodel, each carrying mode (the mean of the per-draw mode vectors of the previous M-step), beta and se (the pooled fixed effects and their standard errors). On the first iteration fits is list() – the callback should return draws from the prior or a starting guess.

m_step_encode

Function function(weights, ...) -> list of blocks. Identical to the contract used by tulpa_em_laplace(): each block is a list with required fields y, X, family, and optional n_trials, offset, phi, re_list, spatial, weights. See ?tulpa_em_laplace for the full spec. A submodel has to keep one latent layout (the length of its mode vector) across draws.

n_mc

Initial number of Monte-Carlo draws per iteration (default 10L).

n_mc_growth

Factor by which n_mc grows after an iteration whose step is swamped by Monte Carlo error (default 4 / 3, Booth and Hobert's 1 + 1/r with r set to 3). 1 keeps n_mc constant.

n_mc_max

Cap on n_mc (default 200L).

max_iter

Maximum EM iterations (default 30L).

tol

Convergence tolerance on the largest change between iterations in units of each coefficient's pooled standard error (default 0.1).

alpha

Level of the confidence ellipsoid that decides whether a step is swamped by Monte Carlo error (default 0.25, Booth and Hobert's choice).

n_consecutive

Number of consecutive iterations delta < tol has to hold for (default 3L).

verbose

Print per-iteration progress (default TRUE).

...

Forwarded to e_step_sample and m_step_encode.

Value

A list with:

  • pooled – named list of pooled per-submodel summaries (mean, se, V_within, V_between, V_total); see rubins_pool().

  • fits – the point estimate in the shape e_step_sample receives: per submodel, mode, beta, se.

  • draws – list of per-MC-draw fit lists from the final iteration, each indexed by submodel name.

  • n_iter – iterations actually run.

  • n_mc_final – n_mc used in the last iteration.

  • converged – logical.

  • inference_mode, inference_tier, target – "structured", 2L, and "Rubin-pooled complete-data Laplace estimates".

  • history – data.frame(iter, n_mc, delta, mcse, swamped): delta the standardized step, mcse the largest Monte Carlo standard error as a fraction of the pooled standard error, swamped whether the step lay inside the Monte Carlo confidence ellipsoid.

Convergence and the Monte Carlo sample size

An MCEM update carries Monte Carlo error, so a rule on the raw change between iterations stalls at the noise floor of the draws however long it runs, and a change relative to |theta| asks for unbounded precision on a coefficient near zero. The rule here follows Booth and Hobert (1999):

  • Step against noise. The Monte Carlo standard error of the pooled update is mcse_j = sqrt(V_between_j / n_mc). When the previous estimate lies inside the 1 - alpha confidence ellipsoid of the update, sum_j (theta_j - theta_prev_j)^2 / mcse_j^2 < qchisq(1 - alpha, P), the EM step is swamped by Monte Carlo error and the next iteration draws n_mc * n_mc_growth (capped at n_mc_max). A step clearly larger than the noise keeps the draw count.

  • Stopping on the posterior scale. The change is measured against the pooled standard error se_j of each coefficient, delta = max_j |theta_j - theta_prev_j| / se_j, and the fit stops once delta < tol on n_consecutive consecutive iterations. A step of tol posterior SDs is small whatever the coefficient's magnitude.

The noise in delta is about sqrt(2) mcse_j / se_j, so tol is also the precision the draws have to reach; history$mcse reports max_j mcse_j / se_j per iteration. A run that ends with n_mc at n_mc_max and delta still at that noise level warns: the cap, not the EM, is what stopped it.

Each M-step fits every draw on its own and averages the per-draw estimates. The fixed point is therefore the mean of the complete-data estimators under p(z | y, theta), which agrees with the EM fixed point (the maximizer of the averaged complete-data log-likelihood) to first order in 1/n.

This is an engine block, not a front door: model packages call it programmatically, so its tuning knobs (max_iter, tol, n_mc) sit in the signature rather than in a control list.

Tier

Tier 2 (structured): complete-data Laplace fits pooled over latent draws. Increasing n_mc reduces Monte Carlo error in the E-step. The fitted modes, Gaussian conditional approximations and Rubin pooling remain the inferential approximation. An exact E-step sampler alone supplies no posterior correction for those approximations.

References

Wei, G. C. G., & Tanner, M. A. (1990). A Monte Carlo implementation of the EM algorithm and the poor man's data augmentation algorithms. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 85(411), 699-704.

Booth, J. G., & Hobert, J. P. (1999). Maximizing generalized linear mixed model likelihoods with an automated Monte Carlo EM algorithm. JRSS B, 61(1), 265-285.

Caffo, B. S., Jank, W., & Jones, G. L. (2005). Ascent-based Monte Carlo expectation-maximization. JRSS B, 67(2), 235-251.

See also

tulpa_em_laplace() for the closed-form-weights variant, rubins_pool() for the pooling rule.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Two-component Gaussian mixture with unit variances: the latent class z is
# sampled in the E-step, and each class mean is an intercept-only Gaussian
# block in the M-step.
set.seed(1)
z <- rbinom(100, 1, 0.4)
y <- ifelse(z == 0, rnorm(100, -1), rnorm(100, 2))

e_step_sample <- function(fits, n_mc, ...) {
  p1 <- if (length(fits) == 0L) {
    ifelse(y > median(y), 0.8, 0.2)
  } else {
    l0 <- dnorm(y, fits$comp0$mode[1], log = TRUE) + log(0.6)
    l1 <- dnorm(y, fits$comp1$mode[1], log = TRUE) + log(0.4)
    1 / (1 + exp(l0 - l1))
  }
  lapply(seq_len(n_mc), function(s) rbinom(length(y), 1, p1))
}
m_step_encode <- function(weights, ...) {
  list(comp0 = list(y = y[weights == 0], X = matrix(1, sum(weights == 0), 1),
                    family = "gaussian"),
       comp1 = list(y = y[weights == 1], X = matrix(1, sum(weights == 1), 1),
                    family = "gaussian"))
}

fit <- tulpa_em_mc(e_step_sample, m_step_encode, n_mc = 5L, max_iter = 8L,
                   verbose = FALSE)
sapply(fit$pooled, function(p) p$mean)
fit$history
# }
